obligations.name: the tab ring visits every reachable control, in document order
a NATIVE NON-DISCOVERABLE unavailable control is skipped by the tab ring
obligations.detail: ["r2","b2"] carry the HTML disabled attribute; focus landed on neither

obligations.name: a DISCOVERABLE unavailable control REMAINS REACHABLE by the tab ring
obligations.detail: ["o3","o4"] carry aria-disabled and no disabled attribute; focus reached ["o3","o4"] — W3C APG: screen reader users are far less likely to discover disabled elements that are not focusable

obligations.name: every focused control paints the indicator at the resolved width
the indicator is the resolved token colour, not a browser default
the indicator is DETACHED at the resolved offset
the dark companion is present outside the indicator
exactly one control carries the indicator at a time
Shift+Tab returns to the previous control
the focus perimeter on an unavailable control is the focus token, NOT dimmed with the control
obligations.detail: o4 focused: rgb(216, 213, 202) at 2px — the perimeter belongs to the input system, and the input system is not unavailable (precedence rule P3)

obligations.name: an AVAILABLE control activates under a real Enter key
obligations.detail: focus landed on b1, which then activated 1 time(s) — without this the obligation below would be vacuous, because a key that activates nothing passes it

obligations.name: a DISCOVERABLE unavailable control CANNOT be activated by the same key
obligations.detail: o4 activated 0, o3 activated 0 — aria-disabled suppresses nothing on its own; MDN: "web developers must manually ensure such elements have their functionality suppressed"

obligations.name: the two availability patterns are VISUALLY IDENTICAL
obligations.detail: DISCOVERABLE o4 rgb(105, 103, 98) · NATIVE r2 rgb(105, 103, 98) · unavailable ink rgb(105, 103, 98) — a visible difference would encode an implementation decision as a Product meaning

obligations.name: SELECTED + UNAVAILABLE keeps the record of the choice and gives up only the ink
obligations.detail: o3 marker present true in rgb(105, 103, 98), weight 600 (selected weight is 600), ink rgb(105, 103, 98) — precedence rule P1: the availability override takes every ink INCLUDING the marker’s, and takes neither the marker’s presence nor the weight

obligations.name: SELECTED + UNAVAILABLE is distinguishable from UNAVAILABLE and from SELECTED
obligations.detail: against UNAVAILABLE o4: marker true vs false, weight 600 vs 500 · against SELECTED o2: ink rgb(105, 103, 98) vs rgb(216, 213, 202)

probes.name: disabled-paint-without-the-attribute
probes.detail: focus reached ["r2","b2"] — the skip obligation MUST reject this

probes.name: outline-removed-with-no-replacement
probes.detail: every stop reported outline-style ["none"] — the visibility obligation MUST reject this

probes.name: discoverable-unavailable-that-still-activates
probes.detail: o4 activated 1, o3 activated 1 — reachable, painted unavailable, and fully operable. The activation obligation MUST reject this

probes.name: only-the-native-pattern-styled
probes.detail: DISCOVERABLE o4 rgb(139, 137, 130) vs NATIVE r2 rgb(105, 103, 98) — the visual-invariance obligation MUST reject this

probes.name: the-override-taking-the-record-too
probes.detail: o3 marker present false, weight 500 vs plain UNAVAILABLE o4 weight 500 — SELECTED + UNAVAILABLE becomes indistinguishable from UNAVAILABLE and the user’s choice is silently rewritten
